chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi'e, from Munzir ibn Jayfar, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Travel during the two cool periods (of the day).' I said, 'We are afraid of the pests (insects/creatures).' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If anything affects you, it is better for you, given that you are guaranteed safety (from the sun/heat), as you are the protected ones.'

key_terms.الْبَرْدَيْنِ: The two cool periods (morning and evening)
key_terms.الْهَوَامِّ: Pests, insects, or small creeping creatures

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on traveling during the day regarding heat and insects?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises traveling during the cooler parts of the day to avoid heat. When asked about fear of insects or pests, he reassures that any harm from them is preferable to the danger of heatstroke, as the travelers are under divine protection.
